response:
The IA is not release-consistent. I’d block on two clustered issues; the remaining findings are follow-ups or likely detector noise.

| Finding(s) | Assessment | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| `permission_ia_drift` (`crime_00011`) | **Blocking** | `/admin` uses `admin`, `manager`, and `owner` inconsistently across navigation, route guards, and documentation. This can expose a destination in nav to users who cannot access it—or hide it from authorized users. Centralize the policy and make nav, guard, and docs consume the same definition. |
| `parallel_destination` + billing orphans (`crime_00003`, `00005`, `00006`) | **Blocking as a cluster** | `/admin/billing-plans` and `/billing-plans` express the same apparent intent, yet neither is reachable or documented. Decide which is canonical, redirect or remove the other, and wire the surviving destination into the intended journey. Reviewing these as three independent low/medium findings would understate the issue. |
| `concept_alias_drift` + organisation/workspace orphans (`crime_00002`, `00007`, `00008`) | **Follow-up**, unless all terms mean the same product object | `organisation`, `team`, and `workspace` coexist, while `/organisation` and `/workspace` are unreachable. Confirm the domain model, select a canonical user-facing term, and retire or deliberately document aliases. Escalate to blocking if these are accidental duplicates rather than distinct concepts. |
| Docs command drift (`crime_00013`) | **Blocking for documentation quality** | `docs/routes.md` advertises `iaq teams`, `iaq workspace`, and `iaq refresh`, but the CLI only exposes `get` and `list`. Readers will receive deterministic command failures. Update/remove these references before treating the documentation as publishable. |
| `/admin` broken-link report (`crime_00004`) | **Likely false positive / detector follow-up** | The detector appears to interpret the application route `/admin` as a filesystem link. Since `src/routes/admin.ts` exists and other findings recognize `/admin` as a destination, this is not sufficient evidence that the route is broken. Verify the Markdown syntax, then report detector feedback if it is an application URL. |

The duplicated `action_label_drift` and `copy_ia_drift` findings (`crime_00009` and `00010`) describe one underlying copy issue—`archive`/`delete`/`remove`—and fall outside the requested route/nav/docs scope. Treat them as one non-blocking copy-system follow-up.

`missing_agent_context` and `dependency_provenance_gap` are valid repository concerns but not IA-consistency findings. The undeclared runtime `commander` dependency may independently block release/install verification, but it should not affect this IA review’s verdict.
